title: A Jev that can ask Opus for help gives Opus accuracy at 4x lower cost
why_read: Discusses a practical technique where a smaller/cheaper model calls a stronger model only when needed, cutting costs while preserving accuracy.
analysis: This item describes an approach where a lightweight agent escalates to a more capable model (Opus) only for difficult cases, achieving similar accuracy at a fraction of the cost. This kind of selective routing or cascading between cheap and expensive models is a genuinely useful engineering pattern for production LLM systems. The high comment count suggests active technical discussion about cost-performance tradeoffs in deploying LLMs. Worth reading for anyone building LLM-based agent pipelines who cares about inference cost.
